programme.title: A Summer Journey with Angela Rippon
programme.sub-title: The Kennet and Avon Canal: The River Kennet
programme.desc: Angela Rippon sets off from Reading to travel the length of the Kennet and Avon Canal. Along the way, she stops off at the Reading Abbey ruins, cycles to the listed Monkey Marsh Lock to view the restoration work taking place there and visits the Littlecote Roman villa.

programme.title: The Flying Archaeologist
programme.sub-title: Hadrian's Wall: Life on the Frontier
programme.desc: Following the first full aerial survey of Hadrian's Wall, archaeologist Ben Robinson flies over it to reveal a new view of its history. He explores a landscape of hundreds of sites of human occupation that suggest the area was richly populated and far from being a barren military landscape. There is also new evidence of Roman occupation earlier than previously thought.

programme.title: Churchill: When Britain Said No
programme.desc: Documentary covering Winston Churchill's failure to be re-elected following the Second World War. Just weeks after VE day, Britain's great war leader Winston Churchill found himself in another battle - to be elected prime minister.

programme.title: The Improbable Mr Attlee
programme.desc: Prof David Reynolds tells the story of Labour's postwar government and examines the achievements of Clement Attlee, including the introduction of the NHS in Britain.

programme.title: Patrick Marber Remembers... After Miss Julie
programme.desc: After years of success in comedy, writing for programmes like `The Day Today', Patrick Marber took many by surprise when he revealed in 1995 that his next project was `After Miss Julie'.

programme.sub-title: The Kennet and Avon Canal: Into Wiltshire
programme.desc: Angela Rippon continues her journey along the Kennet and Avon canal, starting from Hungerford, on the border between Berkshire and Wiltshire, where she finds out how people have come to terms with the 1987 massacre. She continues west to Crofton, where she visits the historic pumping station, and then travels through the Vale of Pewsey before arriving at one of the wonders of the canal world, the Caen Hill Locks in Devizes.

programme.title: The Flying Archaeologist
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson flies over the Thames to uncover new discoveries about WW1, including a network of trenches on The Hoo peninsula next to the former Chattenden Barracks, which were revealed on recent aerial images of the area.

programme.title: The Many Faces of...
programme.desc: An entertaining and revealing journey through the career of one of Britain's best loved actors, Dame Helen Mirren. Her portrayal of Jane Tennison in `Prime Suspect' revolutionised British crime drama and made her a household name, but it was her Oscar winning performance as The Queen that propelled her to international stardom.

programme.title: Helen Mirren Remembers... Gosford Park
programme.desc: Helen Mirren looks back on her role in Robert Altman's acclaimed and multi-award-winning 2001 film `Gosford Park', written by `Downton Abbey' creator Julian Fellowes.

programme.title: Gosford Park
programme.desc: The late Robert Altman's Oscar-winning film is ostensibly a murder mystery set in a 1930s English country house, but the director also uses the plot to explore English sensibilities of the time. A stellar cast all shine without overpowering this very English film from one of America's best directors.

programme.title: The Good Liar
programme.desc: Career con artist Roy Courtnay can hardly believe his luck when he meets well-to-do widow Betty McLeish online. While Betty opens her heart and home to him, Roy walks the most treacherous tightrope of his life as he hatches a scheme to swindle her.
